A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GUARD work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding equations, tables, and figures can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Stable Diffusion experiments, including memorization and image-quality measurements, component ablations, non-memorized prompt evaluation, and runtime results.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds inference-setting ablations, DINO retrieval measurements, full-benchmark evaluation, SD v3.0 results, and GPU-memory measurements.

M1.justification: The GUARD guidance equation, statistical spike detector, attention-logit attenuation, and batched inference procedure are unchanged. The SD v3.0 evaluation does not document a new algorithmic component or a changed mitigation procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Webster's memorization benchmark and the non-memorized LAION prompts for the same text-to-image memorization tasks. The added full-500 evaluation changes filtering within the existing benchmark; SD v3.0 changes the evaluated model rather than introducing a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: Existing comparisons retain their baseline sets. Newly added comparisons use narrower selections: SD v3.0 Table 9 includes RTA, Wen, and Han but explicitly excludes Ren as inapplicable, while the CFG-scale-1 comparison in Table 4 includes only Wen and no mitigation. No new mitigation baseline family is introduced.

E3.justification: v2 adds tests across samplers, 30/50/70 denoising steps, guidance schedules, and CFG scales; DINO@1/@5 evaluation; and peak-memory measurement. It also evaluates all 500 prompts and introduces SD v3.0 testing on 39 prompts selected using SSCD > 0.3. These substantially expand the evaluation protocols while retaining the original filtered experiments.

E4.justification: The existing attention-block, head, timestep, positive-target, and non-memorized-input analyses are retained. New Section A.6 tests the complete CA-in-GUARD method's sensitivity to inference choices; Sections A.7.3–A.7.4 examine dependence on the similarity metric and prompt filtering. Figures 5 and 14 add qualitative case comparisons.

E5.justification: Both versions specify four generated images per prompt and report means with 95% confidence intervals for SSCD and CLIP, without FID intervals. Additional result rows use the existing uncertainty-reporting style; no changed run count, seed policy, significance test, or estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: The original main and detailed result tables retain their numerical values. v2 adds substantial results, including full-benchmark CA-in-GUARD SSCD scores of 0.201 and 0.137 for SD v1.4/v2.0, and SD v3.0 SSCD of 0.168 versus Han's 0.200. DINO, inference-ablation, memory, and qualitative findings are also new. These are additional evaluations, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The mathematical method definitions and equations are retained, with no new theorem, proof, or formal assumption. The added CFG discussion restates the existing guidance equation and interprets its behavior.

C1.justification: The framework, detector, and attention-attenuation contributions remain unchanged. Section 7 adds a claim of the first memorization-mitigation evaluation on SD v3.0, and the conclusion explicitly extends the cross-architecture performance claim to SD v3.0.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation for weaker mitigation at CFG scale 1, attributing it to reduced prompt-conditioned guidance and intervention headroom. It also qualifies transfer to SD v3.0: memorization is weaker on the reused benchmark, and the U-Net mechanistic analysis may not transfer directly. The original white-box-access limitation is retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies DDIM and CFG scale 7.5 as the main experimental defaults and supplies GPU-memory profiles. The batching implementation, original hyperparameter ranges, hardware disclosure, and code-access information remain unchanged. Detailed SD v3.0-specific implementation instructions are not added.

R1.justification: v2 adds Jeon et al. (2025) and discusses its complementary probability-landscape perspective, and adds Caron et al. (2021) for DINO evaluation. It also introduces the SD v3.0 evaluation novelty claim. The broader positioning against training-time, unlearning, and inference-time approaches remains stable.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 groups the original block/head/timestep analyses under A.5, adds subsections for new evaluations, moves the impact statement before the references, adds acknowledgements, and updates the publication footer. This is localized reorganization rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands and reorganizes the displays: the framework diagram moves into the main text, Figure 1 changes from a single row to a larger 2-by-2 arrangement, and several appendix plots are enlarged. New qualitative and robustness figures and new evaluation tables are added. The runtime table is redesigned around per-example time and memory; retained plot contents are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the empirical support for the paper's robustness claims. The new inference ablations, DINO evaluation, and unfiltered benchmark results directly test dependencies on the default sampler configuration, similarity metric, and prompt selection that v1 left largely unresolved. Qualitative comparisons and memory measurements improve practical assessment. The SD v3.0 evidence remains limited to 39 prompts and lacks detailed transfer implementation, but the broader validation provides a substantial net improvement while preserving the original evidence.
